claim: In the relational first-order group language with equality, a named identity \(e\), and ternary \(R(x,y,z)\) for \(xy=z\), the class of all nontrivial finite groups of prime exponent has exactly six quantifier-rank-two theories. Representatives are \(C_2\), \(C_2^2\), \(C_3\), \(C_3^2\), \(C_5\), and \(C_7\). The first four are isolated according to exponent and whether their order equals the prime; all groups of exponent \(5\) and order greater than \(5\) are rank-two equivalent to every group of prime exponent at least \(7\). The largest smallest representative has order \(9\), sharp within this class. This includes nonabelian groups of prime exponent.
integrity: Proof is self-contained; finite checker is corroborative rather than infinite proof.
scientific_limitations: Only finite nontrivial groups of prime exponent in equality, named identity, relational multiplication. No function symbol or higher quantifier-rank conclusion. Literature overlap not ruled out.
title: Six two-round theories of finite groups of prime exponent
